Theorem
[Parameterized Leray--Schauder theorem] 1. ch11:11.6\group gt-ch11 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0298, gilbarg-trudinger:page-0299 Let $T:\B \times [0,1]\to \B $ be compact and satisfy $T(x,0)=0$. If some $M$ satisfies \begin{equation} \tag {11.17} \| x\| _{\B }<M \end{equation} whenever $x=T(x,\sigma )$, then $T_1(x)=T(x,1)$ has a fixed point.
Proof

\sketch Normalize $M=1$. On the closed unit ball, interpolate between the maps $x\mapsto T(x/(1-\varepsilon ),1)$ and $x\mapsto T(x/\| x\| ,(1-\| x\| )/\varepsilon )$ near the boundary. The resulting compact map sends the boundary to $0$, so the radial retraction argument has a fixed point $x_\varepsilon $. For $\varepsilon =1/k$, compactness gives a limit $(x,\sigma )$. If $\sigma <1$, then $\| x\| =1$ and $x=T(x,\sigma )$, contradicting (11.17). Thus $\sigma =1$ and $x=T(x,1)$.

□
